data.title: Missed Star Bulk Carriers' Run? Here's What Early Buyers Saw
data.description:

For Star Bulk Carriers shareholders, the return from the start of the year was 41.8%, including dividends. That outcome naturally invites a look back. If you were weighing the bullish urbanization and fleet-modernization story against the bearish decarbonization and aging-vessel worries, which side of that argument would feel more convincing today?

The Argument You Would Have Been Weighing Up On Star Bulk Carriers

The shares cost US$19.22 at the start of the period, and anyone looking at Star Bulk Carriers then had two clear stories to consider.

The bullish narrative pointed to a Fair Value of US$22.25, built on the idea that global urbanization and longer trade routes could support higher dry bulk volumes and better fleet utilization over time.

The bearish view put Fair Value at US$18.15 and focused on decarbonization and an aging fleet, with tightening environmental rules expected to push capital spending and operating costs higher.

What The Results Changed For The Star Bulk Carriers Thesis

The clearest new fact was the Q3 2026 report. Star Bulk Carriers booked US$366.9 million of revenue and US$141.9 million of net income, with net margin rising from 7.0% in Q3 2025 to 38.7%. That shift backed the bullish profitability assumption, while the need for equity issuance in Greece to fund vessel investments kept the cautious view on capital demands alive. Overall, the evidence cut both ways.

The useful takeaway is where to look first. When a story hinges on margin expansion, track net margin and capital raising side by side. That helps you test whether better earnings quality is coming from the core business or from taking on more financial risk.

What Today's Star Bulk Carriers Price Already Assumes

Star Bulk Carriers now trades at US$25.74. The analyst consensus Narrative on Simply Wall St places its Fair Value above that level, based on a view that current pricing treats the cash return model as fragile.

The same Narrative leans heavily on fleet efficiency and tight vessel supply as the engine for resilient cash generation. A buyer today would need to judge whether ongoing fleet upgrades can keep operating margins supported through shipping cycles.

data.title: Alibaba (BABA) Stock Slides Despite Q2 Earnings And AI Gains
data.description:
Alibaba Group walked into this Q2 FY2027 release with the stock already under pressure, down over 32% across the past three months and another 2.7% lower today to about US$81. The headline result was anything but sleepy. Revenue for the quarter reached RMB 271.5b while net income hit RMB 64.5b, powered by a sharp jump in adjusted earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation in the cloud and e commerce engines.

That clash is the story. Price says caution. The earnings print, especially the surge in adjusted profitability, suggests that investors are still re-pricing old worries more than current fundamentals.

  • Revenue (Q2 2027 vs. Q2 2026): RMB 271,519m vs. RMB 247,795m (up about 10%)
  • Net Income (Excl. Extra Items, Q2 2027 vs. Q2 2026): RMB 64,535m vs. RMB 20,990m (up very sharply, more than tripled)
  • Basic EPS (Q2 2027 vs. Q2 2026): RMB 26.99 vs. RMB 9.05 (up very sharply, about 3x)
  • Cloud Adjusted EBITDA Margin (Q2 2027 vs. prior year period): about 14.9% compared with a lower level in the prior-year period, reflecting a stronger margin profile this quarter

Alibaba kept its huge 2030 cloud goal despite new chip curbs. Ask Charlie what Alibaba’s AI cloud targets really hinge on.

Alibaba’s AI Ecosystem Claim Meets Earnings Reality

Alibaba’s multi layer AI ambition, described by alexandru_g3, a Simply Wall St Community investor, now has clearer scorecards from Q2.

"Within the AI value chain, Alibaba already operates across three of the six major layers: cloud infrastructure through Alibaba Cloud, foundation models through the Qwen family of AI models, and AI applications through products such as Quark, DingTalk, Taobao, and the broader Alibaba ecosystem."

The quarter backs up that structure. AI cloud and compute revenue reached RMB 61b with external revenue at RMB 47b and recurring external revenue at RMB 37b. AI related product revenue was RMB 17.9b with triple digit growth for the thirteenth straight quarter, while cloud margin reached about 14.9%.

Bear Concerns On Capital Intensity And Optionality

Bearish investors question whether Alibaba’s sprawling asset base truly adds resilient value under heavy investment and regulatory risk.

"Beyond its operating businesses, Alibaba owns a portfolio of valuable strategic assets. Its approximately 33% stake in Ant Group could be worth around $90 billion if Ant is valued at roughly $270 billion. Alibaba also owns nearly 5% of CXMT, one of China's most important DRAM manufacturers, a stake that could be worth approximately $25 billion if current market estimates are accurate."

The latest figures show net cash of about US$49b and continued heavy CapEx of RMB 50.5b that pushed free cash flow into a RMB 34.5b outflow. AI investments and export control uncertainty keep those optional assets important but unmonetized this quarter.

To properly understand Rengo's profit results, we need to consider the JP¥6.4b gain attributed to unusual items. While we like to see profit increases, we tend to be a little more cautious when unusual items have made a big contribution. We ran the numbers on most publicly listed companies worldwide, and it's very common for unusual items to be once-off in nature. And that's as you'd expect, given these boosts are described as 'unusual'. Assuming those unusual items don't show up again in the current year, we'd thus expect profit to be weaker next year (in the absence of business growth, that is).

But at least holders can take some solace from the 16% per annum growth in EPS for the last three. Of course, we've only just scratched the surface when it comes to analysing its earnings; one could also consider margins, forecast growth, and return on investment, among other factors. data.title: Could Broader Mortgage Score Access Just Shift FICO's Investment Narrative?
data.description:
• FICO reported that Xactus will now offer the monthly FICO Preferred Program to all mortgage industry clients, bundling Classic FICO Score and FICO Score 10T at a wholesale price of US$10 per bureau, per borrower, with extended availability through the XedaLink and SharperLending platforms.
  • The expanded distribution and fixed bundle pricing give Fair Isaac wider reach into mortgage workflows, which could influence how reliably lenders access its high margin Scores business during a period of competitive and regulatory pressure.
  • We will now assess how this broader FICO Preferred Program distribution through Xactus could reshape Fair Isaac's investment narrative for investors.

Fair Isaac Investment Narrative Recap

To own Fair Isaac, you need to believe the Scores franchise can keep pulling in high quality earnings even as mortgage pricing power comes under pressure. According to andre_santos, a Simply Wall St Community investor who wrote the Narrative, the big swing factor is how much profit Fair Isaac keeps from its mortgage related Scores. The Xactus deal looks helpful for keeping FICO scores embedded in lender workflows, but it does not remove competitive or regulatory risk.

The near term catalyst is execution on the Direct Licensing and Preferred Program rollout that andre_santos sees as central to the story, while managing a higher debt load and recent restructuring. The biggest risk remains share or pricing loss to VantageScore in US mortgages, which the fixed US$10 bundle does not fully address. This announcement feels incremental rather than transformational for that debate.

The most relevant recent move is the appointment of Julie May as President of B2B Scores, given how much Fair Isaac still relies on the Scores segment. Her background across product development, fraud, cybersecurity and go to market work lines up with what the Preferred Program and reseller expansion require, especially as lenders weigh using multiple scores in parallel.

If Fair Isaac executes well under May, the Xactus rollout could support the catalysts that andre_santos highlights, such as keeping margins supported by high scoring profitability and making better use of reseller channels. Investors still need to weigh that against the stated risks, like higher leverage, volatile share performance and the possibility that lenders shift more volume toward cheaper alternatives despite these partnerships.

On andre_santos' numbers, Fair Isaac reaches a fair value of US$632.72 a share if revenue compounds at 4.7% a year and the business settles at a 26.0% profit margin. Together, these factors support strong cash generation in the model without relying on the higher growth and profitability seen in earlier scenarios.

data.title: Weak Statutory Earnings May Not Tell The Whole Story For Gakken Holdings (TSE:9470)
data.description:
Following the release of a lackluster earnings report from Gakken Holdings Co., Ltd. (TSE:9470) the stock price made a strong positive move. We did some analysis and found some positive factors that investors might be paying attention to rather than profit.

This technology could replace computers: discover the 20 stocks are working to make quantum computing a reality.

To understand the value of a company's earnings growth, it is imperative to consider any dilution of shareholders' interests. In fact, Gakken Holdings increased the number of shares on issue by 7.6% over the last twelve months by issuing new shares. That means its earnings are split among a greater number of shares. Per share metrics like EPS help us understand how much actual shareholders are benefitting from the company's profits, while the net income level gives us a better view of the company's absolute size. Check out Gakken Holdings' historical EPS growth by clicking on this link.

How Is Dilution Impacting Gakken Holdings' Earnings Per Share (EPS)?

Gakken Holdings has improved its profit over the last three years, with an annualized gain of 8.1% in that time. Net income was down 3.5% over the last twelve months. But the EPS result was even worse, with the company recording a decline of 4.9%. Therefore, the dilution is having a noteworthy influence on shareholder returns.

In the long term, if Gakken Holdings' earnings per share can increase, then the share price should too. But on the other hand, we'd be far less excited to learn profit (but not EPS) was improving. For that reason, you could say that EPS is more important that net income in the long run, assuming the goal is to assess whether a company's share price might grow.

That might leave you wondering what analysts are forecasting in terms of future profitability. Luckily, you can click here to see an interactive graph depicting future profitability, based on their estimates.

The Impact Of Unusual Items On Profit

Alongside that dilution, it's also important to note that Gakken Holdings' profit suffered from unusual items, which reduced profit by JP¥892m in the last twelve months. While deductions due to unusual items are disappointing in the first instance, there is a silver lining. We looked at thousands of listed companies and found that unusual items are very often one-off in nature. And, after all, that's exactly what the accounting terminology implies. If Gakken Holdings doesn't see those unusual expenses repeat, then all else being equal we'd expect its profit to increase over the coming year.

Our Take On Gakken Holdings' Profit Performance

Gakken Holdings suffered from unusual items which depressed its profit in its last report; if that is not repeated then profit should be higher, all else being equal. But unfortunately the dilution means that shareholders now own a smaller proportion of the company (assuming they maintained the same number of shares). That will weigh on earnings per share, even if it is not reflected in net income. Based on these factors, it's hard to tell if Gakken Holdings' profits are a reasonable reflection of its underlying profitability. While it's really important to consider how well a company's statutory earnings represent its true earnings power, it's also worth taking a look at what analysts are forecasting for the future. data.title: Buffalo's (TSE:6676) Problems Go Beyond Weak Profit
data.description:
The subdued market reaction suggests that Buffalo Inc.'s (TSE:6676) recent earnings didn't contain any surprises. However, we believe that investors should be aware of some underlying factors which may be of concern.

AI is about to change healthcare. These 20 stocks are working on everything from early diagnostics to drug discovery. The best part - they are all under $10bn in marketcap - there is still time to get in early.

Examining Cashflow Against Buffalo's Earnings

One key financial ratio used to measure how well a company converts its profit to free cash flow (FCF) is the accrual ratio. In plain english, this ratio subtracts FCF from net profit, and divides that number by the company's average operating assets over that period. This ratio tells us how much of a company's profit is not backed by free cashflow.

Therefore, it's actually considered a good thing when a company has a negative accrual ratio, but a bad thing if its accrual ratio is positive. While having an accrual ratio above zero is of little concern, we do think it's worth noting when a company has a relatively high accrual ratio. That's because some academic studies have suggested that high accruals ratios tend to lead to lower profit or less profit growth.

For the year to September 2026, Buffalo had an accrual ratio of 0.32. Unfortunately, that means its free cash flow was a lot less than its statutory profit, which makes us doubt the utility of profit as a guide. To wit, it produced free cash flow of JP¥1.9b during the period, falling well short of its reported profit of JP¥7.79b. Buffalo shareholders will no doubt be hoping that its free cash flow bounces back next year, since it was down over the last twelve months. However, that's not all there is to consider. The accrual ratio is reflecting the impact of unusual items on statutory profit, at least in part. The good news for shareholders is that Buffalo's accrual ratio was much better last year, so this year's poor reading might simply be a case of a short term mismatch between profit and FCF. As a result, some shareholders may be looking for stronger cash conversion in the current year.

The Impact Of Unusual Items On Profit

The fact that the company had unusual items boosting profit by JP¥1.0b, in the last year, probably goes some way to explain why its accrual ratio was so weak. While it's always nice to have higher profit, a large contribution from unusual items sometimes dampens our enthusiasm. When we crunched the numbers on thousands of publicly listed companies, we found that a boost from unusual items in a given year is often not repeated the next year. And that's as you'd expect, given these boosts are described as 'unusual'. If Buffalo doesn't see that contribution repeat, then all else being equal we'd expect its profit to drop over the current year.

Our Take On Buffalo's Profit Performance

Buffalo had a weak accrual ratio, but its profit did receive a boost from unusual items. Considering all this we'd argue Buffalo's profits probably give an overly generous impression of its sustainable level of profitability. That means a negative accrual ratio is a good thing, because it shows that the company is bringing in more free cash flow than its profit would suggest. That is not intended to imply we should worry about a positive accrual ratio, but it's worth noting where the accrual ratio is rather high. That's because some academic studies have suggested that high accruals ratios tend to lead to lower profit or less profit growth.

NOF has an accrual ratio of 0.24 for the year to September 2026. We can therefore deduce that its free cash flow fell well short of covering its statutory profit. In the last twelve months it actually had negative free cash flow, with an outflow of JP¥10b despite its profit of JP¥42.1b, mentioned above. It's worth noting that NOF generated positive FCF of JP¥24b a year ago, so at least they've done it in the past. Having said that, there is more to the story. The accrual ratio is reflecting the impact of unusual items on statutory profit, at least in part.

The Impact Of Unusual Items On Profit

Given the accrual ratio, it's not overly surprising that NOF's profit was boosted by unusual items worth JP¥7.1b in the last twelve months. While we like to see profit increases, we tend to be a little more cautious when unusual items have made a big contribution. We ran the numbers on most publicly listed companies worldwide, and it's very common for unusual items to be once-off in nature. And, after all, that's exactly what the accounting terminology implies. Assuming those unusual items don't show up again in the current year, we'd thus expect profit to be weaker next year (in the absence of business growth, that is).

Our Take On NOF's Profit Performance

Summing up, NOF received a nice boost to profit from unusual items, but could not match its paper profit with free cash flow. Considering all this we'd argue NOF's profits probably give an overly generous impression of its sustainable level of profitability.
